b: I went to a further-away Home Depot store yesterday, and took a detour on the way home to visit a Lowe’s store to check out their latest Black Friday tool deals.
That Lowe’s store had this new Kobalt 24V Max cordless power tool combo kit.
The store calls this a limited time deal, which is true for all of the Black Friday deal and gift center items. Lowe’s website says this is the “latest release.”
There’s a price difference. The store had it for $99, Lowe’s website has it for $129.
You get a brushless drill, brushless impact driver, 2Ah battery, and a 45W charger.
DIY-grade brushless 2-tool combo kit for $99? That seems like a great value for what you get.
Hold on. Just 1 battery for 2 tools? That’s obviously a cost-cutting measure. We can call it a value compromise to be nice.

A big part of the benefit of buying a 2-tool combo kit with cordless drill and impact driver is being able to swap between the two. You use the drill for making pilot holes, and the impact for driving in the screw, bolt, or other fastener.
I guess you can always buy another battery later.
Home Depot has a Ridgid 2-tool combo kit for $99. You get a cordless drill, impact driver, 2 batteries, charger, and tool bag.

Despite the Kobalt tools being powered by a 24V Max battery, the Ridgid 18V tools have higher max torque specs. Based on that, the Ridgid 18V tools could deliver higher performance than the Kobalt 24V Max tools.
But, the Kobalt tools have brushless motors, which typically translates to higher efficiency. Which you need if you only get 1 battery.

Kobalt Drill: 500 in-lbs max torque, up to 1800 RPM
Ridgid Drill: 525 in-lbs max torque, up to 1800 RPM

Kobalt Impact: 1800 in-lbs max torque, up to 3500 RPM
Ridgid Impact: 1850 in-lbs max torque, up to 2800 RPM
Checking the specs again, the Ridgid delivers more torque, although the Kobalt has a higher max rotational speed.
If I were a DIYer, hobbyist woodworker, or beginner homeowner looking for an economically-priced combo, which would I buy?

The Kobalt has modern tools that are slimmer. The Ridgid tools deliver more torque. The Kobalt kit gives you brushless motors but only 1 battery. The Ridgid tool uses older tech – or at least I presume this because they make no mention of the motor type – but gives you 2 batteries.
Home Depot has the Ridgid deal for $99. Lowe’s has the Kobalt deal for $99 at my closest store, but $129 online.
At $129, the Kobalt isn’t a good value. It looks decent at $99. Better than the Ridgid? In theory, yes. In practice, I’d rather have 2 batteries for these particular tools.
When I use both tools, I swap between them a lot. Having to swap tools and move a battery back and forth? No thank you.

If I have to expense for another battery, it’d be a better option to put the same money up front for a better-equipped combo kit. If I couldn’t do that, I’d accept a step-down in cordless motor tech and go with the Ridgid kit. I think.
Between these two options, and assuming one is shopping at a Lowe’s store or online after they matche the advertised deal price of $99, which would you buy?
